items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: I want to go back and talk to you about your broadcasting days, from a personal level, being on radio. Tell us about your experience, what the shows were like, who the audience was, you think, or just . . . .

To get into that subject, I began also to write about jazz, eventually in my books, but before that, articles for various magazines – jazz magazines. Also classical, of course. Then, when the Jazz Review came in – Martin Williams and I, and Nat Hentoff, we created that magazine. It became, I think, for a while, while it lasted, the leading, most interesting, learned jazz magazine that was around.
